title: Microanalytical Reference Material Development at the USGS: Outlining Historical Progress and Future Directions
content: The expansion of microanalytical techniques to characterize increasingly diverse geologic matrices drives the need for innovation in developing matrix-matched reference materials (RMs). Microanalytical advances are continually improving analytical accuracy and precision, making many in situ techniques both reliable and cost-effective. Conversely, researchers continually grapple with issues and interferences associated with measurements in geological samples [1, 2]. Whether for routine analysis or method development, RMs play a critical role in producing quality geochemical datasets. The microanalytical reference material (MRM) landscape is accompanied by a host of challenges including a lack of interlaboratory and inter-methodological characterizations, the heterogeneity of natural materials, the presence of multiple “preferred values,” and organizing sufficient production and global availability of materials.
